A Small Bobcat (Used), portable saw mill, hammers, chisels, etc. are all relatively inexpensive to buy...so yes I can get all the equipment for $100,000. While I will admit my numbers are estimates there was some thought and research into them. As far as getting everything to the remote site, that is what the SUV/Trailer are for so I can haul everything I need into the site myself.

I am going to do most of the building myself

So how big is this place going to be? How long is it going to take you to build all yourself? If you're going to build it yourself then you won't have any income during that time. If that is the case, "Working Capital" needs to be factored into your business plan and it is entirely absent. Working capital is what you pay yourself while you're doing all this work so that you can eat and take care of your family or whatever. And if you're going to build this yourself, are you an expert in architecture, design, plumbing, electric, masonry, etc? There's a lot that goes into a building. Not to mention all of the skills needed to set up the wind/solar/hydro facilities that you intend to power said resort. There will be a lot of costs surrounding those trades and specialties you need.

A Small Bobcat

Using a small bobcat to clear a piece of land big enough for an entire resort? What about the trees? And the grade of the property? That's not the type of stuff a bobcat was designed for. Bobcats are for small jobs, and dumping landscape rock and stuff. I don't see how it's up to the task of cleaning up and grading a remote piece of land. And again, you can say you're going to fell all the trees yourself and haul them around to your sawmill yourself, but that all takes a massive amount of time and circles back to my comment about working capital not being factored in.

As far as getting everything to the remote site, that is what the SUV/Trailer are for so I can haul everything I need into the site myself.

You underestimate how big some of the wind power products will be and how they are transported. You also might not have all of the timber you need to build the place on site either. There's still tons of things that you will need that are very large and a simple $50k SUV won't be able to haul.

By all means, if you can do it on $350k, do it. More power to you. But if I'm some kind of investor, every single one of those numbers is off. You'd be better sitting down and writing out a legit business plan and seeking financial investors and business partners to make this happen.

Interesting comment from /u/jedberg on HN:

This happens all the time. At reddit we would get requests from law enforcement asking for email addresses and other private information. Luckily in our case we could simply reply that we didn't know, since we didn't require any personal information to sign up and didn't keep IP address logs that long.

But having been on the other side of the coin, investigating computer crime, I can tell you why it happens. It's really easy to make a request for information, and in most cases, the person you're asking will just willingly give it up even though they don't legally have to, either because they want to be helpful or because they don't know about their legal rights. Even if the evidence can't be used to build a case against the person in court, it can still be used to lead down a path towards finding the person and gathering evidence that is admissible.
